summary.intent: Execute Phase 37 (parallel-batch-upload-pipeline) using wave-based parallel execution, implementing SDK batch upload with p-limit concurrency (Wave 1) and Web Worker encryption offload with useDropUpload rewire (Wave 2).
summary.outcome: Phase 37 completed successfully with all 2 plans executed and verified. Both waves delivered: SDK `uploadFiles()` with p-limit(3) concurrency and `encrypt.worker.ts` with Transferable ArrayBuffer zero-copy transfers wired into `useDropUpload`.

repo: Worktree agents don't always update their branch ref even when commits land on the correct HEAD — cherry-picking from the detached HEAD state was needed to recover Wave 2 commits.
The verifier agent can produce false negatives if it runs before cherry-picked commits are visible in the working tree, requiring manual VERIFICATION.md correction.
Phase 37 is the first phase in its milestone — no prior VERIFICATION.md files exist, so the regression gate was skipped.
The project uses p-limit(3) as the concurrency ceiling for batch file uploads in the SDK layer.
Web Worker is destroyed on logout via `destroyEncryptionWorker()` called from `sdk-provider.ts`.

code.finding: uploadFiles() batch method added with p-limit(3) concurrency pool, stale-metadata re-read before folder update, single IPNS publish, and files:batchUploaded event emission.
80-line Web Worker using Transferable ArrayBuffer for zero-copy AES-256-GCM encryption off the main thread.
147-line Promise-based service wrapper around the encrypt worker using correlation IDs for request/response matching.
Rewired to call client.uploadFiles() batch method instead of sequential upload loop; worker-backed encryptFn passed in.
Calls destroyEncryptionWorker() on logout to clean up the Web Worker.

workflow: When worktree agents commit to a detached HEAD rather than updating the named branch ref, the orchestrator must cherry-pick commits by hash rather than merging the branch.
GSD verifier agents should be spawned after confirming all cherry-picked files are visible on the working branch — timing gap between cherry-pick and agent spawn can cause false gap reports.
Manual VERIFICATION.md correction is a valid recovery path when the verifier produces false negatives due to timing; all artifact existence checks should be done before spawning the verifier.
The stash-merge-restore pattern for integrating worktree changes can leave the orchestrator in the worktree directory rather than the main repo — always verify cwd after merge operations.
`gsd-tools phase complete` must be re-run after recovering from a bad merge to ensure ROADMAP.md and STATE.md reflect the correct branch state.

friction: Worktree agent for Wave 2 committed to detached HEAD instead of updating the branch ref, causing the initial merge to miss all Plan 02 commits.
Orchestrator accidentally navigated into the worktree directory during PROJECT.md update, causing commits to land on the wrong branch.
Verifier agent produced false negatives for all 4 Wave 2 artifacts because it ran before the cherry-picked commits were visible, requiring full manual VERIFICATION.md correction.
The bad Wave 2 merge was not detected until after the VERIFICATION.md correction was already applied, requiring a second reset-and-remerge cycle.
Phase complete (`gsd-tools phase complete`) had to be run twice — once prematurely on the wrong branch state, and again after the correct merge.
open_items: The HUMAN-UAT.md workflow was not exercised — verification passed automated checks without human_needed items, so no UAT file was created for Phase 37.
No prior-phase regression tests exist yet (first phase in milestone) — regression gate will become meaningful in subsequent phases.

The worktree detached-HEAD issue is a recurring risk in the GSD parallel execution flow; a more robust branch-ref update check in the executor agent or orchestrator merge step could prevent future recovery cycles.
